basis.open_question: What operational measure defines productivity, and does “10%” mean 10% above today’s level?

baseline_evidence.quote: We currently have six mid-weight developers, so we're lacking leadership.

links.basis: One dedicated technical lead is provisionally assumed to provide leadership coverage for the current team.
Clearer technical direction is provisionally estimated to raise productivity by 8% of today’s level by month three.
Each additional mid-weight developer is provisionally estimated to add 4% of today’s productivity by month three after recruitment and onboarding.
A provisional annual hiring-cost estimate for a Tech Lead is £150,000.
A provisional annual hiring-cost estimate for each mid-weight developer is £100,000.
Higher cost per hire raises total hiring spend.

unknowns: What is the exact launch date within the next three months?
How long would the current six-person team take to complete the launch scope without any hires?
When could a newly hired Tech Lead or developer realistically start, including recruitment, notice period and onboarding?
What productivity measure should be used for the 10% target (for example, completed launch scope per month, cycle time, or engineering output)?
What measurable code-quality condition must be maintained (for example, defect rate, test coverage, or production incidents)?

The £150,000 Tech Lead and £100,000 per-developer hiring-cost estimates are provisional annual-cost assumptions; confirm whether the £200,000 budget covers annual compensation, three-month cash spend, or total hiring cost.
The productivity estimates assume additive effects by the end of month three and no additional diminishing returns or onboarding interaction beyond the stated per-person estimate.
decision_question: Should I hire a Tech lead or two developers to increase productivity by at least 10%, while maintaining code quality?
